ideas.title: 제조업 주당 근로시간(AWHMAN 첫 빈티지) 3개월 확장 -> v1의 1배/현금 구간에서만 3배 재진입 (ADD overlay)
ideas.mechanism: Firms change hours worked before they change headcount, so a rise in the first-print manufacturing workweek is an early sign that real demand is expanding (it is a Conference Board leading-index component). v1 holds 1x or cash whenever the 200-day gate (+-2%), the 20-day vol >40% rule or a macro alarm fires. Some of those states are false alarms for equities: yield-shock alarms during growth-driven reflation (1999, 2009 H2, 2013) and rebounds where the price gate lags (1991, 2003, 2009). Rising hours separate 'yields or volatility up because real activity is recovering' from 'late-cycle or inflation stress'. The overlay only re-arms 3x inside v1's non-3x states and never cuts v1's 3x or its alarm exits. That leaves v1's real-history edge (out for 2000-02 and 2008, when hours were falling) untouched by design.
ideas.new_information: BLS CES average weekly hours of production and nonsupervisory employees in manufacturing (FRED/ALFRED AWHMAN), the intensive margin of labour input, with true ALFRED first vintages back to 1961-11 (checked: vintages 1962-06, 1975-03, 1987-11 and 1999-06 all download, and first prints differ from the latest values, e.g. 1987-09 first 40.4 vs latest 40.8). It is not among the BT1-F1 ALFRED series (PAYEMS/UNRATE/INDPRO/TCU/HOUST/PERMIT/NEWORDER/RETAIL/RSAFS/CPI/PCE/CP/PNFI), the WX1-M1 66 raw signals, the GWZ table or the c3_newinfo E3 scout. A grep of research/wx1, bt1, open_data, ov1 and NONPRICE_INVENTORY finds no AWHMAN or hours use. It is used only state-conditionally (inside v1 non-3x states), not as standalone timing.

ideas.ceiling: Pre-2014 literature: macro-activity predictors have out-of-sample monthly equity-premium R^2 of about 0 (Goyal-Welch 2008), and about 0.5-1% only for forecast combinations (Rapach-Strauss-Zhou 2010). Stock prices themselves lead LEI components such as hours, so most of the information is priced by release. Expected corr with the next-month 3x-vs-deposit outcome inside v1 non-3x blocks is about .05-.10. A plausible on-block hit rate is 55-60% against a non-3x base of roughly 48-52%. The overlay touches at most about 23% of days (v1 is 3x 77% of the time). Best realistic effect: MS1 path +0.2 to +0.8pp (about 16.4-17.0%); real NDX 86-14 from -2 to +3pp. 2009 H2 is the main possible gain; 1994 and 2010-05 are the main risks. It cannot approach 30%: the WX1 ceiling math needs corr ~.30.
ideas.kill_test: PRECOMMIT before any return is computed. Signal: h3 = AWHMAN_v(m) - AWHMAN_v(m-3), taken from the first ALFRED vintage v that contains m, held daily from the first trading day after realtime_start, stale after 45 days. on = h3 >= +0.20 hours, fixed a priori at about 1 SD of 3-month changes and not tuned; no other variant (N=1). Blocks every 21 trading days; label = 3x index beats deposit over t+3..t+23 (G1 label, 2-day delay). Universe = blocks where v1's target on that real basis (L.v1_B) is NOT 3x. Early windows, each tested separately: SPX 1962-1985 (real_spx_55_85 v1 states) and NDX 1986-1999. Pass condition in each window: P(win|on) >= base_non3x + 10pp AND >= 60%, with >= 8 'on' blocks. Signal-only count with latest data: 37 qualifying months in 1986-99 overall, so >= 8 on-blocks inside non-3x states is borderline and may itself kill the test. If both early windows pass, open NDX 2000-01-03..2014-12-31 once under the same rule. If that also passes, run one measure2 variant (B = 3 where v1 B is 1x/cash and on, else v1 B; av23s(.85) brake unchanged). FINAL needs HEADLINE_MS1 > .1616 AND REAL_NDX > .3108, pw_vs_s085 >= .55, and SPX 55-85 not worse than v1 by > 1pp. Caveat to measure: rerun the early test on latest-vintage data and report both, but decide only on first vintages. Any failure means CLOSE and a registry add.
ideas.path_survival: Change-based, 3-month span, monthly with ~1-week release lag, so it falls inside the <6-month band. L.path_series carries the hours series inside the same 250-day blocks. Only the ~3 months after each block join straddle two blocks (about 25% of each block is contaminated, which adds noise but no lead-lag dependence). v1's non-3x states (gate, vol, alarms) are already recomputed on the path. Expected to survive mostly, unlike level-based macro z-scores.

ideas.title: TED 급등 = 은행 자금조달 경색 시작 → v1 3x 깎기 (Eurodollar 3m − T-bill 3m, 1971~)
ideas.mechanism: When unsecured bank funding gets scarce (the Eurodollar deposit rate rises against the T-bill rate), leveraged intermediaries face higher margins and haircuts and sell risky, high-beta assets (Brunnermeier-Pedersen 2009 liquidity spirals; Garleanu-Pedersen 2011 margin-based pricing; Frazzini-Pedersen 2014: TED moves hit high-beta assets). NDX at 3x is the high-beta, high-margin end, so a sudden widening of TED should come before or during the leverage-unwind weeks. v1's credit alarm reads Baa−Aaa, a slow long-bond default spread. TED is a short-end bank-funding price that moves days to months earlier (for example Aug 2007 versus late 2007 for Baa−Aaa). It might catch part of v1's shock years spent in 3x (1990 credit crunch / Gulf, 1997-98, 2011), and on the SPX side 1973-74 Herstatt/Franklin National, 1980 credit controls and 1984 Continental Illinois.

It is strongly and negatively correlated with same-month equity returns, but its 1-month-ahead predictive correlation with index returns is small (|corr| about .03-.08) and the sign is unstable, because spikes often mark policy-backstop bottoms (Oct 1987, Aug 1982, Oct 1998). If it did pass: about +0.3 to +1.0pp on MS1 path (it fires on about 8-12% of v1-3x days and the 21-day change survives the block rebuild) and about −1 to +2pp on real NDX (it could also fire before the Q4-1998 or post-1987 rebounds). Combined-book corr gain over v1 (.165): at most about +.01-.02.
ideas.kill_test: Signal: TED_t = DED3_t − BEY(DTB3_t), where BEY = 100·365·d/(360 − 91·d) and d = DTB3/100. Value dated t is used from t+1. x_t = TED_t − TED_{t−21}. on_t = x_t ≥ 90th percentile of all past x (expanding window, needs ≥504 obs, so usable from about 1973). Once triggered, on stays for 21 trading days after the last qualifying day. Overlay: v1 target 3x → 1x while on. Kill test A: non-overlapping 21-trading-day blocks from each window start. Keep blocks where v1 is at 3x at block start. Label = 3x product (3r − 2rf − 2.45%/yr) beats the deposit (cash rule) over t+3..t+23. ideas.title: 국채 가격 잡음(Hu-Pan-Wang 차익거래 자본 부족) 급등 뒤 해소 → v1 1x/현금을 3x로 올리기
ideas.mechanism: Hu, Pan and Wang (2013 JF) show that the cross-sectional RMS deviation of Treasury note and bond yields from a smooth fitted curve (their 'noise') measures how scarce arbitrage capital is: when relative-value desks and fixed-income hedge funds lose funding, mispricing widens across the whole market (1987, 1994 Askin/deleveraging, 1998 LTCM, 2001, 2007-08). The ADD side uses the reverse: once noise has spiked and then retraced half of the spike, arbitrage capital is flowing back and forced selling is over. Expected returns to bearing risk are high right after liquidity crises (Nagel 2012 'Evaporating liquidity': liquidity-provision returns rise with crisis-time stress; Brunnermeier-Pedersen spiral unwinding). v1 waits in 1x/cash for NDX to retake SMA200+2%, which loses the V-shaped recoveries. A non-price signal that capital has come back could bring 3x in earlier, in the specific post-crisis windows that are v1's re-entry lag.
ideas.new_information: Treasury-market arbitrage-capital scarcity measured from bond mispricing dispersion (HPW noise, daily 1987+, free from the authors). For an optional pre-1987 diagnostic, a self-built proxy: RMS over 2/5/10y of (H.15 CMT on-the-run par yield − Fed GSW off-the-run fitted par yield), daily from 1971 (2y from 1976). Neither series is in v1, M1, BT1 or the T08 499 families. E10 used GSW only for term-premium/forward-spread bond gating, never for fitting errors or equity timing.

ideas.kill_test: Signal: N_t = HPW Noise_bp; value dated t used from t+1. peak_t = max N over t−62..t; base_t = median N over t−251..t (needs 252 obs, so usable from 1988-01). spike_t = peak_t ≥ 2.0 × base_t ('abnormal noise' = doubling, fixed by theory). relief_t = N_t ≤ base_t + 0.5 × (peak_t − base_t) AND the peak is ≥ 5 trading days old. on_t = spike_t AND relief_t. Overlay: when on and v1 target < 3x, set 3x (v1 brake unchanged). Kill test B: 21-day non-overlapping blocks, keep blocks where v1 is NOT at 3x at block start. Label = 3x product beats deposit over t+3..t+23. PASS requires P(label | on) ≥ base + 10pp AND ≥ 60% AND ≥ 8 on-blocks, in BOTH early NDX 1988-01-04..1999-12-31 and unseen 2000-01-03..2014-12-31 (opened once). Fewer than 8 on-blocks in either window = FAIL, no relaxing. Required control (early window, reported first): the same rule with VXO/VIX in place of N; noise on-hit must be ≥ the VIX on-hit, otherwise CLOSE as T02 vol timing. Optional diagnostic, counted in N but not part of the pass decision: the CMT−GSW proxy rule on SPX 1977-1985. N = 1 primary variant (+1 diagnostic). If it passes: measure2 with v1 under the full FINAL bar.
ideas.path_survival: Uses 63-day peak and 252-day median, both relative to the series' own recent history, plus a relief condition that turns on within weeks of a spike and lasts 1-3 months. The information is change-based and fast (< 3 months), so it survives the 250-day block rebuild. The 252-day base breaks at block joins for about the first year of each block. Using L.path_series keeps noise aligned with its own NDX block, so within-block relations hold, and base windows that span a join only add noise, not look-ahead.

ideas.title: 해외 달러 자금 웃돈(Eurodollar 3m − 미국 CD 3m) 급등 → v1 3x 깎기 (Japan premium / 유럽 은행 달러 부족, CIP 베이시스 대용)
ideas.mechanism: When non-US banks cannot raise dollars onshore, they bid up offshore Eurodollar deposits relative to US-issued CDs. This is the economic content of the covered-interest-parity basis and of the 'Japan premium' (1990-91, 1995-98) and the European bank dollar shortage (2007-08, 2011, when US money funds pulled away from French and Italian banks from June 2011, before the August 2011 crash). Global dollar-funding stress forces cross-border deleveraging (Baba-McCauley-Ramaswamy 2009; Coffey-Hrung-Sarkar 2009 on CIP deviations and funding). Several of v1's losing 3x years were foreign-origin funding shocks (1990, 1997, 2011), which US-only alarms (inversion, 10y shock, Baa−Aaa) do not see. Subtracting the CD rate removes the common US bank credit and bill flight-to-quality parts that make TED reactive, leaving the offshore component.
ideas.new_information: Offshore minus onshore dollar bank funding cost, daily from about 1973, as a free long-history proxy for FX-basis / global dollar shortage. Swap-implied FX basis is not free before 2000. Not in v1, M1, BT1 or the T08 families. It is a decomposition partner of idea 1 (TED = (ED − CD) + (CD − bill)). If both are run, count them as one family, N=2, deflated together.

ideas.title: 방향별 체결 시각: v1이 노출을 줄일 때는 다음 날 미국 시가, 늘릴 때는 종가에 체결 (Direction-dependent fill time for v1's own trades)
ideas.mechanism: v1's signal, states and number of trades stay exactly the same. Only the time of day of the fill depends on the trade's direction. Today MS1 fills every trade at the close of t+2. Under the new rule, every exposure DECREASE (3x->1x, 3x/1x->cash, av23s brake step-downs, the yearly tax-payment sale, the sell leg of the year-end harvest) is filled at the OPEN of t+3, so the account carries its old exposure through one more overnight session. Every INCREASE is still filled at the close of t+2, which already captures the overnight. The case for it is the pre-2014 evidence that US index and ETF price returns accrue mostly close-to-open while open-to-close is roughly zero or negative: Cliff, Cooper and Gulen 2008 (SPY 1993-2006), Kelly and Clark 2011 (ETFs including QQQ), and Berkman, Koch, Tuttle and Zhang 2012 (JFQA: attention-driven retail buying at the open pushes opening prices up, so selling at the open and buying at the close is the favourable side). The rule adds no trades and does not shorten the locked 2-day delay; decreases actually get 2.5 days. It is not a prediction rule: the rule has zero free parameters and is fixed from theory.
ideas.new_information: Daily OPEN prices, which split each day's return into overnight and intraday parts. No closed lane used them. MS1 and every lane fill at closes. X38 shifted whole closes symmetrically for entries and exits (delay 1 and 3), which cannot separate the overnight part from the intraday part. c3_invent I12 (gap asymmetry) was closed as 'not computable: no open prices in the pool'. ideas.mechanism: Listed Korean firms that sell new shares publicly (일반공모, or 주주배정 followed by a public offering of the unsubscribed 실권주) fix the offer price by formula 3-5 trading days before subscription. The discount to the reference price is up to 30% for 일반공모 and typically 20-25% for 주주배정. Anyone with an account at the lead broker can subscribe to the public tranche by depositing 100%. Unallocated cash is refunded on the payment date (2-3 days later). Allocated shares list about 1-2 weeks later and are fungible with the old shares. Payoff = allocation x (P_listing / P_offer - 1) - fees. The dates come from the filing (exogenous), and the payoff can only be reached in the primary market: no secondary-market trade gets the offer-price discount. Risks: winner's curse (Rock 1986: cold deals are fully allocated and then fall; hot deals are rationed), dilution drift up to listing, and small-cap distress. The stream holds cash most of the time and is long one or a few small caps for days at a time, so its beta to NDX is near zero. That makes it a candidate filler for v1's cash days (14% of real 1986-2014 days), not a capital-consuming sleeve.

ideas.mechanism: DB pensions, balanced funds and target-allocation mandates rebalance back to fixed stock/bond weights on a calendar schedule, mostly at month-end and quarter-end. When equities beat bonds by a lot over the period to date, these funds must sell equities in the last few days of the period and the first days of the next one. The trade date is fixed in advance, and the size is roughly the stock-bond drift times the AUM of calendar rebalancers. If that selling is not fully arbitraged, NDX should have lower returns in the window right after a large positive drift. The proposed use is a CUT overlay: move v1 from 3x to cash for one 21-day block. Cash is cheaper than 1x because only one product round trip is paid.
ideas.new_information: The new part is the interaction between a large period-to-date stock-minus-bond drift and a fixed rebalancing date, which turns the drift into a forced flow. T04 tested calendar slices without any drift size. T23 (WX1-M1) and T28 (BT1) used own-price and y10 changes as calendar-free atoms, never anchored to days before period end. No registry row covers pension or balanced-fund rebalancing (I searched closed_axes.json for 재조정, rebal, pension, balanced, 연기금: only S15 index add/delete). Honest caveat: each raw input (equity price, 10y yield, calendar) is already used somewhere. The judge may classify this as same-information complexity under brief rule 5. ideas.title: 국채 결제일 순현금 흡수 규모 / Treasury net settlement cash drain (scheduled net new issuance minus maturities, net of Fed purchases)
ideas.mechanism: Treasury auctions settle on scheduled dates. The amounts are known at the auction, and maturing principal is known from when each security was issued. On each settlement date, dealers, money funds and banks pay the net of new issuance minus maturing principal, and dealers fund their new inventory in repo. A large net drain over a 21-day window takes cash and dealer balance-sheet capacity away from risk assets, which should mean lower equity returns in the following block. A net paydown (for example the April tax-season bill paydown, or debt-ceiling bill cuts) returns cash to the market. Size comes from deficits and refunding decisions. Dates and amounts are public before settlement. Use: CUT v1 3x to cash when the deseasonalized drain is large.

New data input: the per-auction accepted amounts with issue and maturity dates from Treasury Fiscal Data (1979-11 onward, 6,737 records to 2014). From these, compute the dollar net cash drain per window, minus the change in Fed Treasury holdings in 2003-2014 so that QE absorption is netted out. Comparison with closed rows:
- T09 tested auction event dates (E3), not sizes.
- X37 excluded Greenwood-Vayanos duration supply, a slow level gating the bond fill (E10 ceiling 27.2%). This idea is a fast cash-flow quantity used to time NDX 3x, not to gate a bond fill.
- X37 also excluded Hartzmark-Solomon dividend reinvestment; this is a Treasury-side analog of that kind of scheduled cash-flow pressure, not a dividend measure.
The calendar component (refunding months, tax dates) is removed by an expanding same-month deseasonalization, so it does not re-test T04.

ideas.title: 해외 단독 긴축 폭 컷 (Foreign-only monetary tightening breadth cut on v1 3x days)
ideas.mechanism: All of v1's macro alarms are US-only: the US 10y-3m curve, the US 10y yield and the US Baa-Aaa spread. Its losing years are sudden shocks while at 3x (1990, 1994, 1997, 2005-06, 2011), and several of them came during tightening by central banks outside the US: BoJ and Bundesbank in 1989-90, BoE, Bundesbank and BoC in late 1997. First-principles reasoning: when foreign central banks tighten and the Fed does not, global dollar and carry liquidity shrinks and capital flows reverse. US yields and US credit spreads may not move enough to trip v1's alarms, so v1 stays at 3x into a liquidity-driven drawdown, and high-beta NDX is hit hardest. The overlay keeps only the part that is orthogonal to v1: it fires only when foreign banks tighten broadly AND the Fed target is not rising. It moves v1 from 3x to 1x. It never adds exposure, so v1's avoidance of 2000-02 and 2008 is untouched.

ideas.ceiling: Literature up to 2014 has nothing direct on foreign policy predicting US stock returns. Jensen-Mercer-Johnson (1996 JFE) and Conover-Jensen-Johnson (1999) find that restrictive monetary environments lower subsequent returns by about 0.5-1%/month, mainly through each country's own policy, with US policy spilling abroad. Rey (2013) describes a global financial cycle driven mainly by the US. Expected orthogonal monthly correlation with NDX next-month returns is about -0.03 to -0.08. On the WX1 ceiling map, adding an orthogonal corr of .05 to v1's ~.165 gives a combined ~.17, about +0.3-0.6pp path at best. The real-history gain hinges on 1990 (Aug-Oct, NDX about -30%) and late 1997. The likely false-positive cost is 2H1989-1H1990, when NDX was rising and v1 was at 3x. Sparse firing: the on-periods in 2000-14 (Aug-Nov 2000, Sep 2006-Aug 2007) mostly fall where v1 is already in cash, so the unseen window may hold fewer than 8 on-blocks at v1-3x.
ideas.kill_test: Pre-register N=1 with no search over thresholds, lookback or membership. Members (9): JP, DE->XM, GB, CA, CH, AU, SE, NO, NZ. For each available member i, d_i(t) = rate_i(t-1) - rate_i(t-1 minus 63 trading days). The signal S(t)=1 iff two conditions hold. (1) #{i : d_i >= +0.25pp} / #available > 0.5, with at least 6 members available. (2) The Fed target change over the same 63 trading days is <= 0. Overlay: on days where v1's target is 3x and S=1, target 1x (locked MS1 2-day execution delay). Kill test A: take non-overlapping 21-day blocks starting on days where v1 is at 3x. Label = 3x product (3r - 2rf - 2.45%/yr) beats deposit over t+3..t+23. PASS A requires P(label | S=1) <= P(label | all v1-3x blocks) - 10pp, with >= 8 S=1 blocks, in BOTH the early window 1986-01-02..1999-12-31 AND the unseen window 2000-01-03..2014-12-31. The unseen window is opened once, after PRECOMMIT.md + sha256. SPX 1955-85 (discount-rate proxy for the US leg) is reported only. If A passes: run measure2 with the same fixed rule. The external indicator goes through L.path_series in the HEADLINE convention. The input is a 63-day change, so at least ~75% of each 250-day block is free of join artefacts. FINAL = HEADLINE_MS1 > 0.1616 AND REAL_NDX > 0.3108, pw_vs_s085 >= .55, and SPX 55-85 not worse than v1 by more than 1pp. Expected point of failure: the >= 8 on-block count or the 1989 false positives.
ideas.path_survival: Mostly survives. The input is a 3-month (63-trading-day) change of discrete administrative rates, not a level z-score. Within a 250-day block, only the first 63 days depend on pre-block history, so about 75% of block days carry a clean signal. Policy cycles last 6-18 months, so an on-episode often fits inside one block. Two risks: level jumps at block joins could create false 'tightening' flags in the first 63 days of a block if levels rather than the indicator are path-rebuilt (PRECOMMIT must fix which one, following the L.path_series convention). The signal is also sparse, so the path pool may contain few on-days.

shortlist.mechanism: Hu, Pan and Wang (2013 JF) measure arbitrage-capital scarcity as the RMS deviation of Treasury note and bond yields from a smooth fitted curve ('noise'). It spikes when relative-value desks lose funding (1987, 1990, 1994, 1998, 2001, 2007-08). After noise has doubled against its own 1-year median and then given back half of the spike, arbitrage capital is returning and forced selling is over. Expected returns to bearing risk are high right after liquidity crises (Nagel 2012; Brunnermeier-Pedersen 2009, spiral unwinding). v1 waits in 1x/cash until NDX retakes SMA200+2%, so it re-enters V-shaped recoveries late. This input uses neither NDX price nor the alarms and acts only inside v1's non-3x states: it can bring 3x in earlier, and it never cuts v1's 3x or its alarm exits.

shortlist.mechanism: v1's signal, states and trade count stay unchanged. Only exposure DECREASES change: they fill at the open of t+3 instead of the close of t+2, so the old exposure is held through one more overnight session. shortlist.signal_spec: surprise_q = the mean over two sectors of Actual DI(q) - Forecast DI(q): large manufacturing (TK99F1000601GCQ01000 - TK99F1000601GCQ11000) and large electrical machinery (TK99F1150601GCQ01000 - TK99F1150601GCQ11000). Forecast DI(q) is the forecast series' value for target quarter q, published in the survey of q-1. Usable date U_q = the first trading day of the 2nd month after q's end month (Mar survey -> May, Jun -> Aug, Sep -> Nov, Dec -> Feb). This is conservative (at least 3 weeks after the usual release) and is never tightened after seeing results. The 2004Q1 surprise is NaN (BoJ continuity break), so the signal stays off until the next release. thr_q = the 33.33rd percentile (numpy linear) of all surprises with U < U_q; it needs >= 20 of them, so the signal is active from about 1979-08. ON(t) = 1 if the surprise of the latest release with U_q <= t is <= its thr_q, held until the next release. Overlay: B_new = 1 where L.v1_B = 3 and ON, else L.v1_B; the brake is unchanged. Path (HEADLINE): build a step index S (cumulative surprises, stepping on each U_q) and a 0/1 release flag F. On dev250_path, the latest surprise at day t is the jump of L.path_series(S) on the last path day j <= t with L.gather(F) = 1, compared with L.gather(thr) on that day. A fixed-lag difference of S is not used because releases are 60-66 trading days apart, so a fixed window would sometimes span two releases. N = 1, with no threshold or lag search.
shortlist.kill_test: Type A (brief section 4, thresholds unchanged). Blocks: the gate._frame grid of 21-trading-day blocks (NDX from 1986-01-02, SPX from 1955-01-03). A survivor goes to measure2 with B_new. lane.mechanism: Hu, Pan and Wang (2013 JF) measure arbitrage-capital scarcity as the RMS deviation of Treasury note and bond yields from a smooth fitted curve ('noise'). It spikes when relative-value desks lose funding (1987, 1990, 1994, 1998, 2001, 2007-08). After noise has doubled against its own 1-year median and then given back half of the spike, arbitrage capital is returning and forced selling is over. Expected returns to bearing risk are high right after liquidity crises (Nagel 2012; Brunnermeier-Pedersen 2009, spiral unwinding). v1 waits in 1x/cash until NDX retakes SMA200+2%, so it re-enters V-shaped recoveries late. This input uses neither NDX price nor the alarms and acts only inside v1's non-3x states: it can bring 3x in earlier, and it never cuts v1's 3x or its alarm exits.
lane.data_plan: (1) HPW Noise_bp daily: https://en.saif.sjtu.edu.cn/junpan/Noise_Measure_2025.xlsx (court check 2026-11-05: HTTP 200). Keep rows dated 1987-01-02..2014-12-31 and drop later rows on read; save the raw file plus MANIFEST.json (sha256, URL, fetch time). (2) VIX control: column 'vix' of jp.mkX(R,M,'NDX') on jp.calendar('1984-01-03','2014-12-31'). (3) v1 states from L.v1_B(std.contexts()[basis]) and the brake from L.v1_parts; labels and block grid from gate._frame('NDX', ..., '1986-01-02'). (4) SPX bases: no noise data before 1987, so they use v1 B ('not covered'). The generator's pre-1987 CMT-GSW proxy diagnostic is dropped (not run, not counted in N). lab 사용: 아니오 (the noise series is not in the lab panel).
lane.signal_spec: N*_t = Noise_bp dated the previous trading day (a value dated d is usable from close d+1), ffilled for at most 5 trading days, else NaN and the signal is off. peak_t = max of N* over t-62..t, with k_t the date of that max. base_t = median of N* over t-251..t (needs 252 non-NaN values, so first usable about 1988-01-04). spike_t = peak_t >= 2.0 x base_t. relief_t = N*_t <= base_t + 0.5 x (peak_t - base_t) AND (t - k_t) >= 5 trading days. on_t = spike_t AND relief_t. Overlay: B_new_t = 3 if on_t and L.v1_B_t < 3, else L.v1_B_t. The av23s(.85) brake and the 2-day execution delay are unchanged. Path (HEADLINE): N_p = exp(L.path_series(log N*, 'dev250_path')). Every comparison above is scale-invariant, so the cumulative log offset at block joins cancels except in windows that straddle a join. Real bases use N* itself. The constants 63, 252, 2.0, 0.5 and 5 are fixed a priori. N = 1.
lane.kill_test: Type B (brief section 4, thresholds unchanged). Blocks: the gate._frame grid of non-overlapping 21-trading-day blocks from 1986-01-02. Label = the 3x NDX product (3r - 2rf - 2.45%/yr) beats the deposit ((rf - 2pp) x 0.846) over t+3..t+23. Universe: blocks where v1's target L.v1_B (real_ndx_86_14) is NOT 3x at block start. base = hit rate of the universe in the window; cond = hit rate of universe blocks with on at block start. PASS B iff cond >= base + 10pp AND cond >= 60% AND >= 8 on-blocks, in BOTH windows: early 1988-01-04..1999-12-31 and unseen 2000-01-03..2014-12-31 (opened once, after PRECOMMIT.md + sha256). Fewer than 8 on-blocks in either window = FAIL, with no relaxing. Binding control, early window, reported first: run the identical rule with VIX in place of N*. If the VIX rule has >= 1 on-block and its cond exceeds the noise cond, CLOSE as T02 vol timing. A survivor goes to measure2 with B_new. FINAL PASS = HEADLINE_MS1 > 0.1616 AND REAL_NDX > 0.3108, path pw_vs_s085 >= .55, SPX 55-85 not covered (v1 fallback), N = 1 and the deflation stated, glued reported as an upper bound only. Any failure means CLOSE and a registry row.
lane.why_selected: Highest honest p x novelty of the 14 ideas. The input is genuinely new: a mispricing measure built from the Treasury CUSIP cross-section, which no closed lane had. It is fast and change-based, so it survives the 250-day path rebuild. It targets v1's documented re-entry lag on its 23% non-3x days instead of cutting v1's 3x edge, and its relief windows (late 1990, Q4 1998, Q4 2001, spring 2009, late 2011) fall mostly in rebounds. Main risks: (1) only about 3 early episodes, so fewer than 8 early on-blocks and an automatic FAIL are likely; (2) the 1988-99 early window is inside the authors' own sample; (3) the binding VIX control. Court p 0.02 (generator 0.03, cut for the block-count risk). It is the one lane for the funding/arbitrage-stress family, chosen over TED (plumbing-1) and ED-CD (plumbing-3).

lane.title: 방향별 체결 시각: v1이 노출을 줄일 때는 다음 날 미국 시가, 늘릴 때는 종가에 체결 (QQQ 시가 사용, 거래 추가 없음) / Direction-dependent fill time
lane.mechanism: v1's signal, states and trade count stay unchanged. Only exposure DECREASES change: they fill at the open of t+3 instead of the close of t+2, so the old exposure is held through one more overnight session. Pre-2014 evidence: US index and ETF price drift accrues almost entirely close-to-open, while open-to-close is about zero or negative (Cliff-Cooper-Gulen 2008, SPY 1993-2006; Kelly-Clark 2011, ETFs including QQQ). Berkman-Koch-Tuttle-Zhang (2012 JFQA) show attention-driven buying lifts opening prices, so selling at the open and buying at the close is the favourable side. The rule has zero free parameters and adds no trades. The delay for decreases becomes 2.5 days and is never shorter than the locked 2 days.
lane.data_plan: (1) QQQ daily OHLC 1999-03-10..2014-12-31: https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series?symbol=QQQ&interval=1day&start_date=1999-03-10&end_date=2014-12-31&outputsize=5000&apikey=demo (court check 2026-11-05: HTTP 200 with values; split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted), or the same range from the session's already-authorized free-tier Twelve Data connector (get_time_series). (2) SPY daily OHLC 1993-01-29..1999-12-31, for the pre-gate only, from the Twelve Data connector (the demo key returns 401 for SPY). If the connector counts as a login step, record the pre-gate as 'not covered' and proceed on the theory-fixed rule. (3) NDX daily price return r and rf from jp.mkX(R,M,'NDX'), the same r MS1 uses. (4) Engine: a copy of the MS1 engine in the lane's code/ folder (eng2-style, with research/tax_min/code/eng2.py as the template) carrying the split legs. It must reproduce v1 to 1e-12 with on_t = 0 before any split is used. Never use index (NDX/SPX) opens: before 2003 they are stale or missing. lab 사용: 아니오 (needs intraday legs inside the MS1 engine).
lane.signal_spec: No prediction. Split for day t (only where a QQQ open exists, 1999-03-11..2014-12-31): on_t = O_t / C_{t-1} - 1 from raw QQQ prices, with no dividend add-back (the ex-dividend drop lands in the overnight leg, a conservative bias against the rule); id_t = (1 + r_NDX,t) / (1 + on_t) - 1. Product legs: 1x overnight on_t, intraday id_t. 3x overnight 3*on_t, intraday (1 + 3r_t - 2rf_t - 0.0245/252) / (1 + 3*on_t) - 1. Cash overnight 0, intraday the daily deposit rate. Rule: if the executed exposure change due at close e = t+2 is a DECREASE (a v1 step-down 3x->1x or 3x/1x->cash, an av23s brake step-down, or the yearly tax-payment sale), fill it at the OPEN of e+1 instead. The account earns old position x the overnight leg of e+1, pays 0.3% on the traded value at the open, then earns new position x the intraday leg of e+1. Increases, unchanged days and the year-end harvest trades fill exactly as in v1, so the harvest stays inside the tax year. lane.title: 해외 중앙은행 동시 긴축 → v1 3배 깎기: BoJ·분데스방크/ECB·BoE 중 2곳 이상이 6개월 안에 25bp 이상 인상 (CUT)
lane.mechanism: Policy-rate hikes by major non-US central banks tighten global funding and carry positions (yen, DM/euro, sterling) and reduce foreign demand for long-duration growth assets. v1's alarms see only US rates and credit (10y-3m inversion, a 1pp rise in the 10y over 6 months, a Baa-Aaa jump), so it can sit at 3x through a synchronized foreign tightening it cannot see. Pre-2014 support: Jensen-Mercer-Johnson (1996 JFE) and Conover-Jensen-Johnson (1999 JBF) find lower stock returns in restrictive monetary environments across countries, and Ang-Bekaert (2007 RFS) find the short rate is the most robust predictor in the US, UK and Germany. The overlay moves v1 from 3x to 1x only while the count is >= 2 and leaves every other state alone.
lane.data_plan: FRED CSVs (court check 2026-11-05: all HTTP 200), cut at 2014-12-31 on read. INTDSRJPM193N: Japan discount rate (IMF IFS, monthly), used through 1985-06. IRSTCI01JPM156N: Japan call rate (OECD MEI, monthly), used from 1985-07. INTDSRDEM193N: Bundesbank discount rate (monthly), through 1998-12. ECBMRRFR: ECB MRO (daily), from 1999-01-01. INTDSRGBM193N: UK Bank Rate (monthly), 1959-01..2013-03, then 0.50 carried to 2014-12-31 (unchanged since 2009-03-05). URL pattern: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=<ID>. v1 states: L.v1_B on real_spx_55_85 and real_ndx_86_14. Labels: gate._frame for both eras. lab 사용: 아니오 (foreign policy rates are not in the lab panel).
lane.signal_spec: For each c in {JP, DE/EZ, UK}, build a change index X_c = the cumulative sum of the source's own period-to-period changes. The change at each splice (JP 1985-07, discount to call rate; DE to EZ 1999-01) is set to 0, so no level jump between sources enters. Availability: a monthly value for month m is usable from the first trading day of m+1; an ECB daily value from the trading day after its date; ffill onto trading days. up_c(t) = 1 if X_c(t) - X_c(t - 126 trading days) >= +0.25 percentage points. ON(t) = sum over c of up_c(t) >= 2. All three series exist from 1959-07, so the first signal is in 1960-01. Overlay: B_new = 1 where L.v1_B = 3 and ON, else L.v1_B; the av23s(.85) brake is unchanged. Path (HEADLINE): L.path_series of each X_c. The rule uses only 126-day differences, so join offsets cancel except in windows that straddle a join. N = 1, with no search over the threshold, window, country set or a '>= 1' variant. The inventor-1 BIS nine-bank 'Fed not rising' variant is merged here and not run.
lane.kill_test: Type A (brief section 4, thresholds unchanged). Blocks: the gate._frame grid of non-overlapping 21-trading-day blocks (NDX from 1986-01-02, SPX from 1955-01-03). Label = the 3x product beats the deposit over t+3..t+23. Universe: blocks where v1's target is 3x at block start. Early window: SPX 1960-01-04..1985-12-31 (real_spx_55_85 v1 B) plus NDX 1986-01-02..1999-12-31 (real_ndx_86_14), pooled with an era-matched base: drop = sum over eras of n_on,era x (base_era - hit_on,era), divided by the sum of n_on,era. NDX-only is reported but does not gate. Unseen window: NDX 2000-01-03..2014-12-31, opened once after PRECOMMIT.md + sha256. PASS A iff drop >= 10pp AND >= 8 on-blocks in BOTH windows. A survivor goes to measure2 with B_new. FINAL PASS = HEADLINE_MS1 > 0.1616 AND REAL_NDX > 0.3108, path pw_vs_s085 >= .55, real SPX 55-85 not worse than v1 by > 1pp (covered from 1960; 1955-59 uses v1 B), N = 1 and the deflation stated, glued reported as an upper bound only. Discount an unseen pass, because the generator knew the 2000 and 2005-07 foreign tightening history. Failure means CLOSE and a registry row.

The data are administrative (never revised, exact dates) and have the longest early window of any survivor (SPX 1960-85 plus NDX 86-99, enough on-blocks). The rule uses only a 6-month change, so it is path-safe, and it needs only FRED. Chosen over inventor-1 (same family) for the longer early window, verified FRED data and an adequate unseen block count (inventor-1 itself expected fewer than 8 unseen on-blocks). lane.title: 단칸 대기업 예측 오차 → v1 3배 깎기: 실제 DI − 직전 조사의 예측 DI (제조업 전체 + 전기기계), 하위 1/3이면 3x → 1x (CUT)
lane.mechanism: Each quarterly Tankan reports, from the same 200+ large Japanese manufacturers, the business-conditions DI for the current quarter and the DI they forecast for the next one. Surprise_q = Actual DI(q) - Forecast DI(q), with the forecast published one survey earlier, is an unrevised aggregate expectation error that needs no paid consensus. A strongly negative value means demand fell faster than these firms expected three months before. That is an unanticipated global manufacturing or electronics shock, reported by firms that make and buy in the tech-hardware cycle. Hypothesis: US tech prices do not fully absorb this foreign non-price information within the 2-day delay, so v1 at 3x does worse over the next 1-3 months. The overlay moves v1 from 3x to 1x while the latest surprise is in its bottom tercile and leaves everything else unchanged.
lane.data_plan: BoJ Time-Series Data Search API (court check 2026-11-05: HTTP 200): https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/api/v1/getDataCode?format=csv&lang=en&db=CO&startDate=197401&endDate=201404&code=TK99F1000601GCQ01000,TK99F1000601GCQ11000,TK99F1150601GCQ01000,TK99F1150601GCQ11000. These are large-enterprise manufacturing actual/forecast and electrical machinery actual/forecast; endDate must be a quarter code. Metadata, including the Dec 2003 to Mar 2004 break note: https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/api/v1/getMetadata?format=csv&lang=en&db=CO (large file, fetch once). Drop any value after the 2014Q4 survey. Never use the FRED copy BSCICP03JPM665S: it is an amplitude-adjusted monthly interpolation, which builds in look-ahead. v1 states: L.v1_B on real_spx_55_85 and real_ndx_86_14. lab 사용: 아니오 (Tankan is not in the lab panel).
lane.signal_spec: surprise_q = the mean over two sectors of Actual DI(q) - Forecast DI(q): large manufacturing (TK99F1000601GCQ01000 - TK99F1000601GCQ11000) and large electrical machinery (TK99F1150601GCQ01000 - TK99F1150601GCQ11000). Forecast DI(q) is the forecast series' value for target quarter q, published in the survey of q-1. Usable date U_q = the first trading day of the 2nd month after q's end month (Mar survey -> May, Jun -> Aug, Sep -> Nov, Dec -> Feb). This is conservative (at least 3 weeks after the usual release) and is never tightened after seeing results. The 2004Q1 surprise is NaN (BoJ continuity break), so the signal stays off until the next release. thr_q = the 33.33rd percentile (numpy linear) of all surprises with U < U_q; it needs >= 20 of them, so the signal is active from about 1979-08. ON(t) = 1 if the surprise of the latest release with U_q <= t is <= its thr_q, held until the next release. Overlay: B_new = 1 where L.v1_B = 3 and ON, else L.v1_B; the brake is unchanged. Path (HEADLINE): build a step index S (cumulative surprises, stepping on each U_q) and a 0/1 release flag F. On dev250_path, the latest surprise at day t is the jump of L.path_series(S) on the last path day j <= t with L.gather(F) = 1, compared with L.gather(thr) on that day. A fixed-lag difference of S is not used because releases are 60-66 trading days apart, so a fixed window would sometimes span two releases. N = 1, with no threshold or lag search.
lane.kill_test: Type A (brief section 4, thresholds unchanged). Blocks: the gate._frame grid of 21-trading-day blocks (NDX from 1986-01-02, SPX from 1955-01-03). Label = the 3x product beats the deposit over t+3..t+23. Universe: blocks where v1's target is 3x at block start. Early window: SPX 1979-08-01..1985-12-31 (real_spx_55_85 v1 B) plus NDX 1986-01-02..1999-12-31, pooled with an era-matched base: drop = sum over eras of n_on,era x (base_era - hit_on,era), divided by the sum of n_on,era. NDX-only is reported but does not gate. Unseen window: NDX 2000-01-03..2014-12-31, opened once after PRECOMMIT.md + sha256. PASS A iff drop >= 10pp AND >= 8 on-blocks in BOTH windows. A survivor goes to measure2 with B_new. FINAL PASS = HEADLINE_MS1 > 0.1616 AND REAL_NDX > 0.3108, path pw_vs_s085 >= .55, real SPX 55-85 not worse than v1 by > 1pp where covered (1979-08..1985; v1 B before that), N = 1 and the deflation stated, glued reported as an upper bound only. Failure means CLOSE and a registry row.

No closed lane had this construct, and it is path-safe (one quarterly change). It is the weakest pick. The generator's own format check found no negative surprise in 1990, so v1's 1990 loss would be missed, and no pre-2014 study shows foreign surveys predicting US returns (Rapach-Strauss-Zhou 2013 find the US leads). fn.note:
Audit of lane OV1-D. I checked the hashes and the six possible fault areas, then re-ran the test independently in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user--/edfcf3b1-5f4e-5ebe-a258-4da862436b37/scratchpad/aud.py (MS1 venv), without the lane's s2 script so nothing was written to the ledger.

1. **Precommit match.** The sha256 of PRECOMMIT.md (4e83e9db..), tankan_sig.py (96c1748a..), s2_killA.py (2b3d3309..) and the cut CSV (89ff7673..) all match the values frozen in PRECOMMIT. The code follows the spec in section 4 exactly: the mean of (A-F) for manufacturing and electrical machinery, 2004Q1 set to NaN, an expanding-window np.percentile(…, 33.33) over releases with an earlier U and at least 20 prior, ON when surprise <= thr, held until the next release.

2. **Forecast/actual alignment (the main false-negative risk).** In the BoJ series, F(q) is closer to A(q-1) than to A(q). The mean absolute gap is 5.25 vs 5.95 for manufacturing and 7.27 vs 9.01 for electrical machinery, and corr(F, A lagged) is higher than corr(F, A) in both. Spot check: F(2001Q1) = 7 against A(2000Q4) = 10 and A(2001Q1) = -5. So F(q) is the forecast made one survey earlier for q, and the surprise is aligned correctly.

3. **Point in time.** The signal uses information known at close t and is conservatively late. There is no look-ahead: 2014Q4 is dropped, and the data end at 201404.

4. **Label.** gate._frame scores True when the 3x product (3r - 2rf - 2.45%/yr) beats the deposit over t+3..t+23. A CUT signal needs hit_on below the base rate. The observed hit_on is above the base (SPX .727 vs .561; NDX .600 vs .569), so the sign really is the opposite of the hypothesis and is not inverted by the code.

5. **v1 states.** I used the same Ctx construction as std.contexts(). Early blocks are mostly v1-3x: NDX {3x: 137, 1x: 17, cash: 14} and SPX {3x: 41, 1x: 18, cash: 17}, which fits the brief's 77% of days at 3x.

6. **Could a perfect signal have passed?** Yes. There are 178 universe blocks and 61 on-blocks, far above the minimum of 8, and the base rate is about .56, so a drop of 0.10 or more was reachable.

**Recompute.** My independent run reproduced n_on 11 + 50 = 61, an era-matched drop of -0.0551 and pass_A = False exactly, with the release table and thresholds identical.

**Lag diagnostic (not counted).** With every release moved 25 or 45 days earlier, the drop was -0.020 and -0.022. It stays negative, so staleness is not the cause.

The ON periods match the builder's account: 1982-83, late 1985 to 1986, 1992-94 and 1997-99. The signal was OFF in October 1987 and in 1990, so it missed the losses v1 is meant to avoid.

The unseen window was not opened, and I opened no forbidden files. Verdict: the fail is real and not an artifact.
